newsitem.title: USA: FERC oks Nautilus Gulf Mex natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: FERC oks Nautilus Gulf Mex natgas pipeline.

text.p: Nautilus Pipeline Co LLC said Wednesday it has has received regulatory approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) and is moving forward with construction of the $121 million Nautilus natural gas pipeline in the central Gulf of Mexico.
Nautilus is owned by affiliates of Shell Oil Co (50 percent), Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners LP (25.67 percent) and Marathon Oil Co (24.33 percent).
The company said construction of the 101-mile, 30-inch pipeline is anticipated to begin in early April and is expected to be completed by November 1997.

The pipeline, with a capacity of 600 million cubic feet of gas per day, will connect with the Manta Ray Offshore Gathering System at Ship Shoal Block 207 and extend onshore to Exxon's Garden City gas plant in southern Louisiana for redelivery to multiple onshore transmission lines.
Shell and Marathon have committed significant gas supplies to the project and Nautilus has received total commitments of nearly 300,000 mcf/day so far.
Marathon will oversee construction of the pipeline and onshore facilities.
